A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACTIONREASONINGBENCH. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning results, ramification experiments, and human ratings of question naturalness.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds binary ramification results, input-format experiments, and supplementary scoring analyses.

M1.justification: The four-stage PDDL/ASP question-generation and paraphrasing pipeline, ramification construction, and separate binary/free-answer fine-tuning procedures are retained. The additional evaluations do not introduce a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The same eight domains and six question categories remain. v3 extends evaluated scenarios to PDDL and templated inputs in Appendix K and binary questions with ramification constraints in Table 4; v2 reported ramification results only for free answers.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B, and the GPT-4o/o1-preview ramification pairing. Added experiments reuse these models; newly cited benchmarks are not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds supplementary protocols: Appendix K samples 10% of the test set for input-format experiments, and Appendix F evaluates free answers with F1-BERTScore. The original splits, sequence lengths, prompting conditions, accuracy evaluation, and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix K introduces input-format sensitivity tests using PDDL and templated language. Appendix F adds concrete cases where BERTScore undervalues a correct paraphrase or rewards an incorrect answer. Detailed domain and fluent breakdowns also supplement previously discussed analyses, substantially expanding diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors of the mean using the same stated formula. New tables extend this reporting practice without introducing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy tables retain their values after relocation. Substantial new results appear in Tables 8–10, 15, 17, and 18. Table 4 adds GPT-4o binary ramification accuracies of 80.95%, 57.14%, and 57.14% at sequence lengths 1, 10, and 19, alongside unchanged zero free-answer accuracy. These are additional conditions and results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The fluent definitions, transition-function description, PDDL specifications, and state-space complexity expressions (1)–(8) are retained in renumbered appendices. No new formal derivation or proof is introduced; the added complexity discussion interprets empirical behavior.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same benchmark contribution, coverage, complex-question performance deficit, and headline ramification claims. The shortened conclusion does not redefine the contribution. Notably, the zero-success claim for GPT-4o remains unqualified despite the newly reported binary successes.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking inconsistent state-space complexity trends to different LLM heuristics, PDDL performance to pretraining, and templated-input advantages to reduced verbal reasoning demands. Appendix F discusses semantic-similarity scoring failures. The existing six limitations are largely retained, moving from Section 7 to Appendix A.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly clarifies that model evaluations exclude external tools and formal solvers. Table 4 explains missing responses as resulting from longer prompts. These are limited disclosures; existing hardware, optimizer, epochs, batch settings, context limit, and evaluator prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands the RAC-versus-planning comparison and discusses parallel ACPBench, adding Natural Plan and TravelPlanner references. New analyses cite McCoy et al. and BERTScore. Guan et al. (2023) and Valmeekam et al. (2024b) are removed, while PlanBench remains. The central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Related work is locally rewritten, selected explanations are refined, and the conclusion is shortened. Limitations move to Appendix A, the results appendix gains subsections, and acknowledgements and publication headers are added. Most methodological and appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a fluent-category plot, six supplementary result tables, and two scoring-example boxes. The ramification table expands to separate free-answer and binary columns. The original binary accuracy table moves into Appendix C, while the existing question-category plot is retained as Figure 3. These substantially expand and reorganize the evidence displays.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously discussed domain and fluent behavior more auditable and adds useful tests of input-format sensitivity and scoring failures. These provide a limited improvement in diagnostic support. Important reporting problems constrain the gain: the abstract and conclusion still imply universal GPT-4o ramification failure despite Table 4's binary successes, and Appendix K does not report a matched natural-language baseline for its sampled subset.
